It is also called ``Senda Shrine'' or ``Osenda-san'' after the name of the place where it is enshrined.

It is located halfway up Mt. Nakao, a hill in the southern part of Senda, Arita City, facing south.

== About the enshrined deity ==

headed to ``Ne no Kenshu Province, where Susano no Mikoto is seated,'' he first aimed for ``Kuni no Kuni'' (the ancient name of Kii Province). In other words, Kii is envisioned as the entrance to Nekenshu Province (Ne no Kuni), and there is a relationship between ``Susanoo no Mikoto'' who sits in Ne no Kuni and Kii's ``Susa God'' (our company's enshrined deity) at the entrance.<ref group="Note">In "Kojiki," it is {{ill|Oyabiko|ja|大屋毘古神|zh|大屋毘古神|qid=Q10935046}} of the Boku no Kuni region who sent Oanamutsokugami to Susanoo, the land of roots, but this god is said to be the same god as Susanoo's child god, Isotake no Kami. </ref>. {{ill|Takeshi Matsumae|ja|松前健|qid=Q11529297}}, looking at this together with our company's sea god-like nature, speculates that our company is the origin of the Susanoo faith that spreads all over the country, and that the original deity is the one who visits at set times to bring fertility from the land of roots, which is {{ill|UNKNOWN|lt=eternal country}} across the sea.<ref name="Matsumae"/> (See later section "{{ill|UNKNOWN|lt=Appendix}}").

These three deities are said to be the gods who brought wood seeds to Kii Province, and in Kii, they are collectively known as the ``Ita-ke-so Sanjin'', and each is located at (Kiso), {{ill|Oyatsuhime Shrine|ja|大屋都姫神社|qid=Q11434556}} (Udamori, Wakayama City), and {{ill|Tsumatsuhime Shrine|ja|都麻都比売神社|qid=Q17216259}} (3 Ronsha shrines). Our company has a particularly deep relationship with Itakeso Shrine, and our (Private)|Q11589711|Kobe}} is said to have been located adjacent to Itaigeso Shrine (see the later section "{{ill|UNKNOWN|lt=History}}"), and it is said that the shrine's members visited during festivals, and historical sources from {{ill|Muromachi period|ar|فترة موروماتشي|ast|Periodu Muromachi|bcl|Panahon nin Muromachi|be|Перыяд Мурамаці|bg|Муромачи|bn|মুরোমাচি যুগ|ceb|Panahon sa Muromachi|ckb|سەردەمی مرۆماچی|cs|Období Muromači|de|Muromachi-Zeit|eo|Epoko de Muromaĉi|es|Período Muromachi|eu|Muromachi aroa|fa|دوره موروماچی|fi|Muromachi-kausi|fr|Époque de Muromachi|gl|Período Muromachi|he|תקופת אשיקאגה|hu|Muromacsi-kor|id|Zaman Muromachi|ilo|Panahon ti Muromachi|it|Periodo Muromachi|ja|室町時代|kk|Муромачи кезеңі|ko|무로마치 시대|lt|Muromači laikotarpis|nl|Muromachiperiode|pl|Muromachi (okres)|pt|Período Muromachi|ru|Период Муромати|simple|Muromachi period|sk|Obdobie Muromači|sl|Obdobje Muromači|sr|Муромачи период|sv|Ashikaga|th|ยุคมูโรมาจิ|tl|Panahong Muromachi|tr|Muromachi Dönemi|uk|Період Муроматі|vi|Thời kỳ Muromachi|wuu|室町时代|zh|室町时代|zh_min_nan|Muromati sî-tāi|zh_yue|室町時代|qid=Q334845}}<ref group="Hara">{{ill|Yoshida Kanetomo|arz|يوشيدا كانيتومو|de|Yoshida Kanetomo|fr|Yoshida Kanetomo|ja|吉田兼倶|ko|요시다 가네토모|pt|Yoshida Kanetomo|ru|Ёсида Канэтомо|zh|吉田兼俱|qid=Q723266}} "Shinmeicho headnote". This Kobe is identified as the area around Kuchi-Susa and Oku-Susa in Wakayama City, which borders Ita-Kiso Shrine.{{Sfn|Susa-Kobe (Taira)|1983}}<ref group="Note">According to the ``Kanei-ki'' included in ``Ki Meisho Zue'' and ``Ki Tsuzuki Fudoki,'' this Susa-Kobe existed until the early modern period. </ref>. Susa Shrine, the former Mukakusha, once existed in Kuchisusa (Kuchisusa Kamienmanji Temple, {{Coord|34|11|55.8|N|135|14|38.3|E|region:JP-30_type:landmark|name=Susa Shrine Ruins (Susa Kobe Estimated Site)}}). == Shinto priest ==
Since the Middle Ages, our company's {{ill|Shake (social class)|id|Shake (kelas sosial)|ja|社家|qid=Q11588367}} has been held by the Oga clan (in olden times, they used the surnames Oe and Iwahashi).

== Precincts ==
[[File:Susa-jinja (Arida) keidai.JPG|thumb|250px|right|Full view of the temple grounds. The approach is from left to right at the bottom of the image. On the upper right are the main shrine, oryoden, worship hall, and bell gate. ]]``The main hall'' is made of Ikkensha Sumikiri {{ill|Kasuga-zukuri|es|Kasuga-zukuri|fr|Kasuga-zukuri|ja|春日造|ru|Касуга-дзукури|qid=Q3193781}} and has a copper plate roof. The front pillar space is 1 ken, but the back and sides are 2 ken, and corner blocks are placed on the front pillars, which is a structure that follows the Kumano-zukuri style. </ref>. This was done by order of the feudal lord, {{ill|Tokugawa Yoshimune|ar|توكوغاوا يوشيمونه|ca|Tokugawa Yoshimune|cdo|Dáik-chiŏng Gék-cŭng|cs|Jošimune Tokugawa|de|Tokugawa Yoshimune|es|Tokugawa Yoshimune|eu|Tokugawa Yoshimune|fa|توکوگاوا یوشیمونه|fr|Tokugawa Yoshimune|hak|Tokugawa Yoshimune|hr|Yoshimune Tokugawa|id|Tokugawa Yoshimune|it|Tokugawa Yoshimune|ja|徳川吉宗|ko|도쿠가와 요시무네|ms|Tokugawa Yoshimune|pl|Yoshimune Tokugawa|pt|Tokugawa Yoshimune|ro|Tokugawa Yoshimune|ru|Токугава Ёсимунэ|simple|Tokugawa Yoshimune|sk|Jošimune Tokugawa|sr|Токугава Јошимуне|sv|Tokugawa Yoshimune|th|โทกูงาวะ โยชิมูเนะ|tr|Tokugawa Yoshimune|uk|Токуґава Йосімуне|uz|Tokugava Yosimune|vi|Tokugawa Yoshimune|war|Tokugawa Yoshimune|zh|德川吉宗|zh_classical|德川吉宗|zh_min_nan|Tokugawa Yosimune|zh_yue|德川吉宗|qid=Q319664}}. (Japan)|Q1193848|Mashinori}} It was rebuilt in September of the first year ({{ill|1711|ab|1711|af|1711|als|1711|am|1711 እ.ኤ.አ.|an|1711|ar|1711|ary|1711|arz|1711|ast|1711|avk|1711|az|1711|azb|۱۷۱۱ (میلادی)|ba|1711 йыл|ban|1711|bar|1711|bcl|1711|be|1711|be_x_old|1711|bg|1711|bn|১৭১১|bo|༡༧༡༡ལོ།|bpy|মারি ১৭১১|br|1711|bs|1711.|ca|1711|cdo|1711 nièng|ceb|1711|ckb|١٧١١|co|1711|crh|1711|cs|1711|csb|1711|cv|1711|cy|1711|da|1711|de|1711|diq|1711|el|1711|eml|1711|eo|1711|es|1711|et|1711|eu|1711|fa|۱۷۱۱ (میلادی)|fi|1711|fo|1711|fr|1711|frp|1711|frr|1711|fur|1711|fy|1711|ga|1711|gan|1711年|gcr|1711|gd|1711|gl|1711|gv|1711|he|1711|hi|१७११|hr|1711.|hsb|1711|ht|1711 (almanak gregoryen)|hu|1711|hy|1711|hyw|1711 թուական|ia|1711|id|1711|ilo|1711|io|1711|is|1711|it|1711|ja|1711年|jv|1711|ka|1711|kaa|1711|kk|1711 жыл|kn|೧೭೧೧|ko|1711년|krc|1711 джыл|kv|1711 во|la|1711|lb|1711|lez|1711 йис|li|1711|lij|1711|lmo|1711|lt|1711 m.|lv|1711. gads|mai|१७११|map_bms|1711|mdf|1711|mg|1711|mhr|1711|mi|1711|min|1711|mk|1711|mr|इ.स. १७११|mrj|1711 и|ms|1711|my|၁၇၁၁|myv|1711 ие|mzn|۱۷۱۱|nah|1711|nap|1711|nds|1711|new|सन् १७११|nl|1711|nn|1711|no|1711|nrm|1711|nso|1711|oc|1711|olo|1711|or|୧୭୧୧|os|1711-æм аз|pa|1711|pl|1711|pnb|1711|pt|1711|qu|1711|ro|1711|ru|1711 год|rue|1711|sa|१७११|sah|1711|sc|1711|scn|1711|sd|1711ع|se|1711|sh|1711.|shn|1711|si|1711|simple|1711|sk|1711|sl|1711|smn|1711|sq|1711|sr|1711|su|1711|sv|1711|sw|1711|szl|1711|ta|1711|te|1711|tg|Соли 1711|th|พ.ศ. 2254|tk|1711|tl|1711|tr|1711|tt|1711 ел|uk|1711|ur|1711ء|uz|1711|vec|1711|vi|1711|vls|1711|vo|1711|wa|1711|war|1711|wuu|1711年|xmf|1711|yi|1711|zh|1711年|zh_classical|一七一一年|zh_min_nan|1711 nî|zh_yue|1711年|qid=Q6866}}), and the Nakamura family, the head carpenters of the Kishu clan, was involved in its construction, and it appears that it was directly managed by the clan.<ref name="Arita Catalog">"Arita Regional Cultural Properties Catalog", Arita Regional Cultural Properties Protection Deliberation Committee Liaison Council, 1997. </ref>. On three sides of the front side of the main building, there is a rim with a raised railing (large floor), and side shoji screens are installed at the rear of both sides. The interior is divided into the {{ill|Presbytery (architecture)|an|Presbiterio (arquitectura)|be|Прэзбітэрый|be_x_old|Прэзьбітэрыюм|bg|Презвитерий|br|Chantele|ca|Presbiteri|cs|Kněžiště|el|Ιερό Βήμα|eo|Antaŭaltaro|es|Presbiterio (arquitectura)|eu|Presbiterio|ga|Saingeal|gl|Presbiterio|hu|Presbitérium (szentély)|id|Panti imam|it|Presbiterio|ja|内陣|ko|제단 (건축)|lt|Presbiterija|lv|Presbitērijs|mk|Презвитериум|pl|Prezbiterium|pt|Presbitério|ro|Prezbiteriu|ru|Пресвитерий (храм)|sh|Prezbiterij|simple|Chancel|sk|Presbytérium (priestor v kostole)|sl|Prezbiterij|sr|Презвитеријум (простор у цркви)|sv|Presbyterium|th|บริเวณคริสต์ศาสนพิธี|uk|Пресбітерій|qid=Q14616641}} and the outer hall by installing front and rear partitions on the central column of the main building, and a board door with a scroll, but it is said to be unusual in that the outer hall floor is one step higher than the kirikina nagaoshi and lower than the edge. Although there are few decorations such as carvings and the paintings are modest, it has a dignified appearance and is a valuable relic that shows the style of the Nakamura family <ref name="Overview"/>. This main shrine has been designated as a cultural property designated by Arita City.In front of the main shrine are the ``Chumon Gate'' and the ``Oratory Hall'', which are connected to the ``Oratory Hall''. The middle gate is a flat {{ill|UNKNOWN|lt=Karamon}}, the hall of worship is a flat {{ill|East Asian hip-and-gable roof|de|Irimoya|es|Tejado de gabletes de Asia oriental|fr|Irimoya-zukuri|ja|入母屋造|ko|팔작지붕|ru|Иримоя-дзукури|uk|Напіввальмовий дах|zh|歇山顶|qid=Q855025}} with 3 girders and 2 beams, and the worship hall is a gabled tsumairi with 1 beam and 3 girders, and both have copper plate roofs. The hall of worship and the hall of worship are both open-air. The hall of worship is lower than the hall of worship, and the hall of worship has an upper floor in the center. The ``Suzumon'' (four-legged gate) standing in front of the shrine is {{ill|Kirizuma-style|zh|悬山顶|qid=Q13308575}} flat and {{ill|UNKNOWN|lt=tiled roof}}. In addition, there are shrine buildings such as Kama-dono, {{ill|Kagura-den|es|Kaguraden|fi|Kaguraden|fr|Kagura-den|it|Kagura-den|ja|神楽殿|qid=Q94498}}, and Ema-do hall in the precincts.

== Festival ==

== Annual festival ==
* Monthly Festival (1st day of every month)
*Monthly Festival (14th of every month)
* Saitan Festival (January 1st)<ref>Description of annual festivals is based on the shrine history book. </ref>
* Congee fortune telling (January 15th)
*Setsubun Festival (February 3rd)
* Lecture (February)
* Spring Festival (Prayer Year Festival) (March)
* Big catch festival (April)
* Summer Purification (June)
* Summer Festival Yoimiya (July 13th)
* Summer Festival (July 14th)
* Wakoshi (June 30th of the lunar calendar)
* Senda Festival (October 14th)
* Winter Festival (Ninamesai) (November)
* Great purification ceremony (December 31st)

It is said that it was once so popular that people would say, ``If you want to see a bride, then it's the Senda Festival'' {{Sfn|Susa Shrine (Corner)|1985}}, and even today it is also called the ``Senda Fighting Festival'' because fishermen fiercely compete for the sea bream thrown at them, believing that whoever gets it will be blessed with a big catch for a year. Afterwards, we eat red bean porridge and pray for good health throughout the year.

According to ``Zoku Fudoki,'' until the Tensho period (the end of the 16th century), 12 sacred horses were dedicated from Itageso Shrine at the Senda Festival, and priests from the company participated in the ritual, and 12 priests from the company also visited the shrine every year on the first day of the New Year. It is thought that these were rituals in which the company's enshrined deity (Isotake no Mikoto) had an audience with his father deity {{Sfn|Susa Shrine (Gods; First Edition)|1986|p=350-352}}.

== Important cultural property (designated by the country) ==
* Tachi inscription: Inshu Jukagecho 1 mouth (with Itomaki Tachi Koshirae)<ref name="arida"/>*: It was dedicated in 1721, 50 years after the death of the founder of the Kii Tokugawa clan, {{ill|Tokugawa Yorinobu|eo|Tokugawa Yorinobu|es|Tokugawa Yorinobu|fa|توکوگاوا یورینوبو|fr|Tokugawa Yorinobu|ja|徳川頼宣|ko|도쿠가와 요리노부|pt|Tokugawa Yorinobu|ru|Токугава Ёринобу|uk|Токугава Йорінобу|zh|德川賴宣|qid=Q1045763}}, by Yoshimune Tokugawa, Yorinobu's grandson and the eighth shogun. It was created by Kagenaga, a {{ill|Japanese swordsmith|ja|刀工|qid=Q91012922}} of {{ill|UNKNOWN|lt=Inshu}} (currently {{ill|Tottori Prefecture|ace|Prefektur Tottori|af|Tottori-prefektuur|an|Prefectura de Tottori|ar|توتوري (محافظة)|arz|محافظة توتورى|az|Tottori prefekturası|azb|توتوری اوستانی|ban|Préféktur Tottori|be|Таторы (прэфектура)|bg|Тотори (префектура)|bn|তোত্তোরি প্রশাসনিক অঞ্চল|ca|Prefectura de Tottori|cdo|Tottori-gâing|ce|Тоттори (префектура)|ceb|Tottori-ken|ckb|پارێزگای تۆتۆری|cs|Prefektura Tottori|cy|Tottori (talaith)|da|Tottori-præfekturet|de|Präfektur Tottori|eo|Gubernio Totoro|es|Prefectura de Tottori|et|Tottori prefektuur|eu|Tottori (prefektura)|fa|استان توتوری|fi|Tottorin prefektuuri|fr|Préfecture de Tottori|frr|Tottori (Prefektüür)|ga|Maoracht Tottori|gl|Prefectura de Tottori|hak|Tottori-yen|he|טוטורי (מחוז)|hr|Tottori (prefektura)|hu|Tottori prefektúra|hy|Տոթթորի (պրեֆեկտուրա)|id|Prefektur Tottori|ilo|Prepektura ti Tottori|it|Prefettura di Tottori|ja|鳥取県|jv|Préfèktur Tottori|ka|ტოტორის პრეფექტურა|ko|돗토리현|lt|Totorio prefektūra|lv|Totori prefektūra|mk|Тотори (префектура)|mni|ꯇꯣꯠꯇꯣꯔꯤ ꯂꯝꯈꯥꯢ|mr|तोतोरी प्रांत|ms|Wilayah Tottori|my|တော့တိုရိခရိုင်|ne|तात्तोरी|nl|Tottori (prefectuur)|no|Tottori (prefektur)|oc|Prefectura de Tottori|os|Тоттори (префектурæ)|pl|Prefektura Tottori|pnb|ضلع ٹوٹوری|pt|Tottori|ro|Prefectura Tottori|ru|Тоттори (префектура)|sd|توتوري پريفيڪچر|se|Tottori prefektuvra|sh|Prefektura Tottori|simple|Tottori Prefecture|sk|Tottori (prefektúra)|sr|Префектура Тотори|su|Tottori Prefecture|sv|Tottori prefektur|sw|Mkoa wa Tottori|tg|Префектураи Тоттори|th|จังหวัดทตโตริ|tl|Prepektura ng Tottori|tok|ma Totoli|tr|Tottori (prefektörlük)|tt|Тоттори (префектура)|uk|Префектура Тотторі|ur|توتوری پریفیکچر|vi|Tottori|war|Tottori (prefektura)|wuu|鸟取县|zh|鳥取縣|zh_classical|鳥取縣|zh_min_nan|Tottori-koān|zh_yue|鳥取縣|qid=Q133935}}) during the Muromachi period. The figure of the sword is slender, the base iron is koitame, and the blade pattern is a thin straight blade (hoso-suguha), which is typical of Yamashiroden. ``Wakayama Prefecture Cultural Properties Guidebook'', Wakayama Prefecture Board of Education, 1999. </ref>. A tachi with a blade length of 63.6 cm and a length of 2.2 cm. The blade pattern is clove. Dedicated by {{ill|Tokugawa Munenao|ja|徳川宗直|ko|도쿠가와 무네나오|zh|德川宗直|qid=Q6993442}}. The Koshirae was made in the Edo period, and both the {{ill|grip|ja|柄|qid=Q19508474}} and sheath are made of purple thread. The metal fittings show {{ill|Hishi mon|ja|菱紋|qid=Q11620223}} painted in red bronze.The scabbard is decorated with {{ill|Maki-e|es|Maki-e|fr|Maki-e|hu|Maki-e|id|Maki-e|it|Makie|ja|蒔絵|ka|მაკი-ე|ko|마키에|ml|മാകി-ഇ|mr|मकि-इ|pl|Maki-e|ru|Маки-э|sl|Maki-e|zh|蒔繪|qid=Q2083390}}, and the metal fittings and the Aoi crest (Aoi crest|Q11353976}}) are arranged alternately<ref name="Arita catalog"/><ref name="arida"/>.

The monument was erected in November 1979 to commemorate his visit to our company on that occasion and the poem he wrote, ``This is the shrine of the gods of Iketaru, the kingdom of time, and the shrine of the gods of Fukaburo.'' Standing in front of the third torii gate.

Shimane|zh|出雲市|zh_classical|出雲市|zh_min_nan|Izumo-chhī|zh_yue|出雲|qid=Q825166}})]]Not only Susa Shrine, there are many shrines in {{ill|Izumo|ja|出雲|qid=Q11395836}} and Kii that have the same company name (see the table on the right). Regarding this, there is a theory that both originated in Izumo and that the Izumo people brought their home country's religion with them when they settled in Kii. </ref>, there is a theory by Ken Matsumae and others that considers Kii to be the original homeland. Regarding Susanoo, it has been pointed out from an early stage that there is a discrepancy between the inner nature of Susanoo as a god of destruction and tyranny as seen in the Kiki and the inner nature as {{ill|Culture hero|als|Kulturheros|ar|بطل ثقافي|bg|Културен герой|cv|Культурăлла герой|de|Kulturheros|es|Héroe cultural|he|גיבור תרבות|id|Pahlawan budaya|it|Eroe culturale|ja|文化英雄|ko|문화 영웅|la|Heros culturae|lt|Kultūrinis herojus|nl|Cultuurheld|no|Kulturhelt|os|Культурон хъайтар|pl|Bohater kulturowy|pt|Herói cultural|ru|Культурный герой|simple|Culture hero|tr|Kültürel kahraman|uk|Культурний герой|zh|文化英雄|qid=Q977690|lt=Bunka Hero God}} as seen in ``{{ill|Izumo no Kuni Fudoki|de|Izumo Fudoki|ja|出雲国風土記|simple|Izumo-no-Kuni Fudoki|zh|出雲國風土記|qid=Q11395858}}'', and various theories have been proposed. </ref>.According to Ken Matsumae's theory, if Susanoo, which appears in both the Kojiki, Nihon Shoki, and Fudoki, is viewed as a separate entity, the deep kinship with the ocean-like and tree-like divinity and the land of roots seen in the Kojiki cannot be found in the Fudoki, but it can be seen in the Kii Company. From this, we infer that the Susanoo mentioned in the ``Kojiki'' and ``Nihonshoki'' refers to the deity enshrined at our company. He also cites the theory that the Land of Nenes, an ``eternal country'' in the Kii region where Susano-o is said to visit, was equated in the central government with Nekuni, which is the ``source of disaster'' and ``the land that sends back disasters,'' and that Susano-o was also seen as a god of destruction and tyranny that brought disaster. Furthermore, as supporting evidence that Susanoo from the Kojiki and Nihon Shoki is the deity enshrined by our company, we cite the importance placed on it by the Imperial Court, such as the designation of the shrine as a famous deity and records of investitures <ref name="Matsumae"/>.

Regarding the relationship with Izumo, Ken Matsumae also states that some of the Kaijin of Kii, who were honored with Susanoo and engaged in diplomacy with the continent (Korea), settled in Izumo. It is assumed that as the faith in Susanoo spread to the inland areas of the Izumo region, the inner nature of the ocean god etc. was lost. Another theory is that the complexity of Susanoo's divinity arose as a result of the thoughtless reunification of the Susanoo statues that existed in the central aristocracy and the Izumo region at the time of the compilation of the Kiki.<ref name="Matsumae"/>
